To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the copolymerization of EO and oxiranes allows for the preparation of functional PEG copolymer with adjustable lower critical solution temperature behavior.
novel functional PEG copolymer systems with adjustable LCST properties can be obtained by AROP from a versatile monomer toolkit.
a series of novel PEG-based copolymers, obtained by an AROP approach, exhibit LCST behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a novel epoxide monomer library and the investigation of the resulting LCST behavior of the corresponding PEG copolypeptides.
a novel class of stimuli-responsive polymers with a broad LCST range and the possibility of functionalization of the PEG main chain.

the development of a versatile toolkit for the synthesis of novel PEG-based polymers bearing functional groups at the backbone, which can be used as a basis to design new functional materials for a wide range of applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LCST behavior of PEG-based copolymers is mainly determined by their hydrophilic-hydrophobic balance.
the LCST is a complex phenomenon that depends on the polymer architecture and the nature of the side groups.
the LCST of the copolymer is mainly governed by the side chain hydrophobicity, but that the hydrophilicity of the backbone also has a significant influence on the LCST of PEG copolypeptoids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LCST can be adjusted by varying the comonomer ratio of the oxiranes, which is a simple and straightforward approach.
the hydrophobicity of the comonomer side groups is the key factor for the LCST behavior of the copolymers.
the LCST behavior of the investigated copolymers can be controlled by the side group hydrophilicity and the side group density.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the AROP of oxiranes with different side groups can be used to generate a library of functional PEG copolymer systems with adjustable LCST properties, and the LCST behavior is influenced by the hydrophobicity of the functional side group.
AROP of epoxides is a versatile tool to obtain functional PEG-based copolymers and that the LCST can be tuned by the comonomer ratio and the side group hydrophilicity.
the LCST behavior of the PEG copolypeptides can be easily tuned by the choice of the comonomer.
